patch_description: The original algorithm routes every partition of every destination along a single shortest path, causing redundant transfers over shared edges. Inspired by multicast/Steiner-tree ideas and k-shortest-path load balancing, this approach: (1) computes k candidate shortest paths per destination, (2) balances partitions across those candidate paths to spread load and exploit parallel low-cost links, and (3) prefers edges shared with already-planned routes (cheap "piggybacking" on transfers already scheduled), reducing redundant data movement. The result is lower total cost while keeping the same BroadCastTopology output format.
